ai.description: This small snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is glossy dark purple-brown dorsally with a vibrant red venter and tail tip. Key features include a blunt, rounded head and a short, spine-tipped tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Teretrurus sanguineus* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid purple-red venter, which contrasts sharply with its uniform dark brown or blackish dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: *Teretrurus sanguineus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Teretrurus sanguineus* is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Teretrurus sanguineus* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Teretrurus sanguineus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations above 1,000 meters.
